audits.title: Audit of antipsychotic prescribing and monitoring for the management of behavioural and psychological symptoms of dementia
audits.standard: NICE guideline on antipsychotics for behavioural and psychological symptoms of dementia; local CAIR form
audits.setting: Older Persons Community Mental Health Team

cycle1.result: CAIR form present in 73% of notes (37% the new shorter version); 63% of forms fully completed; 100% had assessment of causes, non-drug interventions first, target symptoms and review within 3 months.

audits.other_findings: Risk-benefit discussions were documented vaguely. Teaching held, leaflet to be provided, team to revert to original CAIR form and re-audit in 6 months.
audits.citation: Thomas C, Bhattacharyya S, Bond E. Audit of antipsychotic prescribing and monitoring for the management of behavioural and psychological symptoms of dementia. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(S1):S108-S109. doi:10.1192/bjo.2021.320.

audits.title: Antipsychotic Prescribing for Behavioural and Psychological Symptoms of Dementia: An Audit of Prescribing Practices in the Harrogate Community Mental Health Team for Older Adults
audits.standard: NICE NG97 (2018) Dementia guideline and local trust guidance on antipsychotic prescribing and monitoring
audits.setting: Harrogate Older Adult Community Mental Health Team

cycle1.result: 88% had assessment of sources of distress; 42% had a non-pharmacological intervention before antipsychotic (58% after starting); 63% had documented risk discussion; 63% baseline bloods, 54% baseline ECG; 33% on treatment over 12 weeks had a discontinuation or dose-reduction trial; under 22% had physical health monitoring at one year.

audits.other_findings: Random sample of 24 of 55 patients. Recommended a pre-prescribing checklist and a system to flag when monitoring and review are due.
audits.citation: Wilson J, White N, Croft M, Ahmed S, Illsley L, Hughes P. Antipsychotic Prescribing for Behavioural and Psychological Symptoms of Dementia: An Audit of Prescribing Practices in the Harrogate Community Mental Health Team for Older Adults. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(S1):S187-S188. doi:10.1192/bjo.2023.485.

audits.title: Audit on Management of Behavioural and Psychological Symptoms Among Dementia Patients in Humber Older People's Mental Health Services
audits.standard: NICE: non-pharmacological before pharmacological management; antipsychotics started low and slow; follow-up at least 6 weeks after starting
audits.setting: Humber Older People's Mental Health Services

cycle1.result: About 24% started on medication without trial of non-pharmacological methods; those started on medication were properly followed up; overall adherence around 75%.

audits.other_findings: Risperidone was the commonest medication (37%). Re-audit suggested in 12 to 24 months.
audits.citation: Adeoye S. Audit on Management of Behavioural and Psychological Symptoms Among Dementia Patients in Humber Older People's Mental Health Services. BJPsych Open. 2024;10(S1):S211-S211. doi:10.1192/bjo.2024.523.

audits.title: Quality of Antipsychotics Prescribing in Dementia Patients in Wakefield (WF9 Area)
audits.standard: NICE guidance on antipsychotics in dementia: initiation for severe agitation/distress under specialist supervision, monitoring and follow-up

cycle1.result: 24 of 63 with dementia on antipsychotics; blood monitoring 56% (13/24); ECG 50% (12/24); follow-up plan 81% (51/63); reduction plan 8% (2/24)

audits.other_findings: 8% (5/95) on antipsychotics without dementia diagnosis; an antipsychotic register was suggested.
audits.citation: Piparsania B, Marriott R, Sunder S. Quality of Antipsychotics Prescribing in Dementia Patients in Wakefield (WF9 Area). BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S159-S159. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10424.

audits.title: Prescribing and Monitoring of Antipsychotics for Behavioural and Psychological Symptoms of Dementia in a Community Older Adult Mental Health Service: A Retrospective Audit
audits.standard: Nottingham Area Prescribing Committee guidance EG019 and NICE NG97
audits.setting: Newark and Sherwood Older Adult Community Mental Health Team, Nottinghamshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Target symptoms identified in 100%; delirium considered in 83%; risk of harm documented in 67%; risk-benefit discussion in 83%; review at or before six weeks in 80%; rationale for continuation in 60%; deprescribing considered in 60%; Trust Antipsychotics in Dementia Assessment and Monitoring Form completed in 0%.

audits.other_findings: 114 records were screened and only six met inclusion criteria. Education, better induction and system changes were recommended, with a re-audit planned including baseline physical health monitoring.
audits.citation: Hammed S, Wright R, Davis L, Tomlinson R, Sathian A. Prescribing and Monitoring of Antipsychotics for Behavioural and Psychological Symptoms of Dementia in a Community Older Adult Mental Health Service: A Retrospective Audit. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S298-S299. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11707.

audits.title: Cardiovascular Risk Assessment and Monitoring in Dementia Patients Prescribed Antipsychotics: A Multi-Centre Audit
audits.standard: NICE guidance and local trust policies on cardiovascular assessment, ECG, metabolic monitoring and risk–benefit documentation when prescribing antipsychotics
audits.setting: Three inpatient mental health wards across two hospitals

cycle1.result: BP, heart rate and weight recorded in 19/20; ECG on admission in 8; ECG before or within 72 hours of antipsychotic start in 3; QTc documented in 6; HbA1c checked in 11; ongoing metabolic monitoring in 7; no documented cardiovascular risk–benefit discussion in any case.

audits.other_findings: Medication was reviewed regularly at MDT meetings for all patients. Suggested actions include staff awareness, prescribing checklists and electronic prompts.
audits.citation: Song C, Finlay J. Cardiovascular Risk Assessment and Monitoring in Dementia Patients Prescribed Antipsychotics: A Multi-Centre Audit. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S285-S285. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11737.

audits.title: A Clinical Audit to Review the Use of Antipsychotic Medications in Patients With a Diagnosis of Dementia in Community Mental Health Team for Older Adults in West Essex
audits.standard: NICE guidance on antipsychotics for BPSD: documentation of BPSD, exclusion of causes, non-pharmacological interventions first, structured assessment (ABC chart), review every 6 weeks
audits.setting: Older Adult Community Mental Health Services covering care homes in West Essex (Epping, Uttlesford, Harlow)

cycle1.result: BPSD documentation 100%; investigations to exclude organic causes and delirium 91%; ABC chart 38.5%; initial 6-week review 59 (75.6%); subsequent 6-weekly reviews 43 (55.2%).

audits.other_findings: Documentation of environmental causes and non-pharmacological measures was too unclear to audit. A standardised antipsychotic review record was proposed.
audits.citation: Rao P, Chouliaras L. A Clinical Audit to Review the Use of Antipsychotic Medications in Patients With a Diagnosis of Dementia in Community Mental Health Team for Older Adults in West Essex. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S340-S340. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11831.
